title: Sort to Expose Structure
summary: Pay an up-front sorting cost when global order turns a difficult global comparison into a simple adjacent or frontier scan.
recognition_signals: sorted order makes related values adjacent or creates monotonic frontiers
a later linear scan becomes much simpler after sorting
core_rules: Preserve all metadata required by the output when sorting records.
Use a sort key that exactly matches the requested ordering.
Do not sort when the task only needs membership and a cheaper hash-state solution suffices.
structural_steps: choose the ordering that exposes the needed local relationship
sort records without discarding required fields
scan adjacent items or ordered frontiers
produce the result from the newly exposed structure

common_confusions.distinction: If only presence or duplicate detection matters and extra memory is allowed, hash membership may avoid the O(n log n) sorting cost.
